title: Frontend to Backend: REST and FHIR

answers.question: How do the frontend apps talk to the OpenMRS backend, REST or FHIR? Show me where each is used in the patient management app.

paragraphs.text: Both are used. In this app the default is the **OpenMRS REST API** (via `openmrsFetch` + `restBaseUrl`), with **FHIR2** used for a specific, smaller set of resources — mainly `Location` and `Patient` reads — using `fhirBaseUrl` together with the framework's FHIR hooks. The two are not alternatives at the transport level: `openmrsFetch` is the single fetch wrapper for both, and `restBaseUrl` / `fhirBaseUrl` just pick which base path the URL is built from (both imported from `@openmrs/esm-framework`).

- `restBaseUrl` — REST paths such as `/patient`, `/encounter`, `/obs`, `/cohortm/cohort`, `/appointments`, `/location`, `/concept`.
- `fhirBaseUrl` — FHIR R4 paths such as `/Patient/_search`, `/Location?`.

- **Patient search** builds `` `${restBaseUrl}/patient` `` with `q`, `v` (custom representation), `includeDead`, `limit` [1], and fetches individual patients with `` `${restBaseUrl}/patient/${uuid}?v=...` `` [2].
- **Recently viewed patients** are stored as REST user properties at `` `${restBaseUrl}/user/${userUuid}` `` [3] and written back by POST [4].
- **Registration writes** go entirely through REST: create/update patient, encounters, identifiers, person names and relationships [5], the ID generator [6], and person attributes [7].
- **Registration reads for editing** use REST custom representations: patient identifiers [8], encounters/obs [9], person attributes [10], and person details [11].
- **Patient lists** are REST throughout: the cohort module via `cohortUrl` [12], list queries packages/esm-patient-list-management-app/src/api/patient-list.resource.ts, membership reads packages/esm-patient-list-management-app/src/api/patient-list.resource.ts, and create/edit/delete packages/esm-patient-list-management-app/src/api/patient-list.resource.ts.
- **Ward** uses REST for encounters, beds, patients and obs packages/esm-ward-app/src/ward.resource.ts, a single location packages/esm-ward-app/src/hooks/useLocation.ts, the patient record packages/esm-ward-app/src/hooks/useRestPatient.ts, most recent obs packages/esm-ward-app/src/hooks/useMostRecentObs.ts, admission locations packages/esm-ward-app/src/hooks/useAdmissionLocation.ts and EMR configuration packages/esm-ward-app/src/hooks/useEmrConfiguration.ts.
- **Service queues** use REST for queues packages/esm-service-queues-app/src/hooks/useQueues.ts, queue entries and concepts packages/esm-service-queues-app/src/hooks/useConcept.ts.
- **Appointments** are REST only — no `fhirBaseUrl` appears in that package. Examples: providers packages/esm-appointments-app/src/hooks/useProviders.ts, active visits packages/esm-appointments-app/src/hooks/useActiveVisits.ts, appointment search packages/esm-appointments-app/src/patient-appointments/patient-appointments.resource.ts, appointment writes packages/esm-appointments-app/src/form/appointments-form.resource.ts, and summaries packages/esm-appointments-app/src/workload/workload.resource.ts.

- **Patient list members**: after resolving member UUIDs over REST, the patient details are fetched from FHIR with `` `${fhirBaseUrl}/Patient/_search?_id=...` `` and read from the bundle's `entry[].resource` packages/esm-patient-list-management-app/src/api/patient-list.resource.ts.
- **Ward locations (list/paginated)**: `` `${fhirBaseUrl}/Location?...` `` via `useFhirPagination` packages/esm-ward-app/src/hooks/useLocations.ts.
- **Service queues locations**: queue locations via `` `${fhirBaseUrl}/Location?_summary=data&_tag=queue location` `` packages/esm-service-queues-app/src/create-queue-entry/hooks/useQueueLocations.ts, and session location ancestry via FHIR `Location:partof` chaining with `_include:iterate` packages/esm-service-queues-app/src/hooks/useSessionLocationAncestry.ts.
- **Registration and search location pickers**: `` `${fhirBaseUrl}/Location?` `` with `_summary`, `_count`, `_tag` and `name:contains` search params packages/esm-patient-search-app/src/patient-search-page/refine-search/person-attributes.resource.ts and packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/field/person-attributes/location-person-attribute-field.resource.tsx.

Note that these FHIR calls still go through `openmrsFetch`, except where a framework FHIR hook is used (`useFhirPagination`, `useFhirFetchAll`), which wrap the same fetch internally. Some FHIR calls also mix in REST helpers: the same file uses `restBaseUrl` for concepts and person attribute types packages/esm-patient-search-app/src/patient-search-page/refine-search/person-attributes.resource.ts.
Because some components consume `fhir.Patient` while the data arrives over REST, small mappers exist in between:

- Search results: `mapToFhirPatient(patient)` packages/esm-patient-search-app/src/utils/fhir-mapper.ts, used by the compact banner packages/esm-patient-search-app/src/compact-patient-search/compact-patient-banner.component.tsx and the patient banner packages/esm-patient-search-app/src/patient-search-page/patient-banner/banner/patient-banner.component.tsx.
- Checked-in patients: `mapActiveVisitPatientToFhir` converts a REST `visit.patient` into a `fhir.Patient` packages/esm-service-queues-app/src/create-queue-entry/checked-in-patients/checked-in-patients.resource.ts.
- Registration edit: the reverse direction, `getFormValuesFromFhirPatient` and friends pull form values back out of a `fhir.Patient` packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/patient-registration-utils.ts.

```mermaid

title: Backend access per feature
---
flowchart TD
  subgraph rest["REST API (restBaseUrl + openmrsFetch)"]
    search["Patient search"]
    reg["Registration writes"]
    lists["Patient lists / cohorts"]
    ward["Ward encounters and beds"]
    queues["Service queues"]
    appts["Appointments"]
  end
  subgraph fhir["FHIR2 API (fhirBaseUrl)"]
    locs["Location pickers"]
    fhirPat["Patient _search"]
  end
  fhirPat --> lists
  locs --> reg
  locs --> queues
  locs --> ward
```

- Practice: REST is the norm for writes and for module-backed domains (appointments, cohorts, queues, ward); FHIR is used for `Location` reads and one `Patient` search, plus the `fhir.Patient` shape that some shared banner components expect.
- One caveat: `restBaseUrl`, `fhirBaseUrl`, `openmrsFetch`, `useFhirPagination` and `useFhirFetchAll` are imported from `@openmrs/esm-framework`, which is not among the repositories I could read here, so their internals are not verified from source — only their use inside this app is.
